scope: Remepy SharePoint and OneDrive accessible through the connected account; tenant-wide keyword search plus direct folder browsing and current file/version checks. This is not an exhaustive inspection of every tenant file.
findings: Protocol.xlsx is a later detailed full-app weekly schedule (revision 22.0, 8 Oct 2026), but an explicit supersession of the Product draft was not found.
The current Product daily-schedule workbook is revision 5.0, modified 1 Nov 2026. Both sheets still explicitly label all values as draft placeholders.
psychological program V0.xlsx is actively maintained despite its filename: latest revision 154.0, 1 Nov 2026. Its core session timeline matches the local CSV previously compared.

The latest dedicated May psychology specification found is revision 329.0, 6 Aug 2026. Itay's onboarding document says changes have since been made and links List Psych PD.xlsx as the detailed asset list.

List Psych PD.xlsx is revision 286.0, 26 Oct 2026. Its first sheet includes app day 1 onboarding without Mindset and Welcome on app day 2; this is a different numbering scheme from psychology session IDs.

The 31 Oct device description specifies about 30 minutes daily. During the logged medication window it recommends Practice, then Play, then Mindset; otherwise Mindset, Play, Practice. Users can choose any incomplete section.
The heavy-speech entries in Protocol.xlsx total 31 minutes on schedule days 1, 3, 5 and 7; 30 minutes on days 2, 4 and 6.

Newer implementation material includes Psychology context pages (1 Nov), Psychology audio items trailers (31 Oct), and prepages_month1 activities (28 Oct). These supplement the earlier spec rather than proving an approved replacement.
No changes made to the intervention, source files, videos, or Lab journey.

excerpts.device_daily_overview:
is information is used by the app to identify the mobility & balance practice workout difficulty levels (e.g., ‘Base’, ‘Active’, ‘Max’) that are presented as available options to the user prior to each workout (further described in Section 6.3.3). Users who report a history of falls are not presented with the Max difficulty level.
Setting Reminder for a Morning Routine – An optional set up of a daily notification reminder that will prompt the user to complete the guided morning routine practice from the library. The morning routing is further described in Section 6.4.4.
Daily Overview – Practice / Play / Mindset Screen (Day 2+)
The daily overview can be accessed from a tile on the home screen or from the navigation bar. Beginning on the user’s second full day of treatment, it presents the day’s activities organized into category sections for Practice, Play, and Mindset, each displaying the approximate time needed to complete and progress. The app recommends an activity category for the user to start with, based on the timing of their last logged IR CD/LD medication dose. Within the IR CD/LD dosing window, Practice is recommended first, followed by Play, then Mindset. Outside the IR CD/LD dosing window, or when no dose has been logged, Mindset is recommended first followed by Play, then Practice. As section categories are completed, the next incomplete category section is recommended. 
Regardless of the recommended activity, the user can proceed with any incomplete activity section at any time. If a user attempts to complete Practice activities outside of their logged medication window (i.e., 30-150 minutes after IR CD/LD intake), the app presents the user with a non-blocking notice suggesting a different incomplete activity alternative from the daily overview (e.g., Play, Mindset); if no alternative activity remains available, the notice is still presented to inform the user of the timing. For Play activities, the screen preceding the activity always displays text indicating that the activity is recommended to be performed within the IR CD/LD dosing window. These recommendations are intended to support performance of physical and cognitive activities during periods of anticipated therapeutic benefit from IR CD/LD, while also mitigating potential risks associated with physical training during an “off” state (e.g., fall risk).

excerpts.device_mindset:
starting.
“Mindset”
The Mindset category includes four types of activities: informational videos, breathing exercises, audio activations, and gamified activations.
Informational videos introduce the user to specific topics and provide practical guidance and strategies for managing the everyday and emotional challenges of living with Parkinson’s disease. Breathing exercises offer guided instruction in four techniques: box breathing, belly breathing, physiological sigh, and coherent breathing. Audio activations are audio-only sessions that guide the user through mindfulness, relaxation and reflection practices including grounding, guided imagery, and progressive muscle relaxation (PMR). In-the-moment relaxation tools, body scan, awareness of breath, observing thoughts, self-compassion, and self-affirmation. Gamified activations are interactive mini-“games” such as: reflection activation, which prompts the user to bring to mind something they are grateful for, a pleasant experience, or a value-based action and then presents a series of on-screen reflection questions for self-directed contemplation without requiring user input; inner voice, which presents sentences the user must choose to embrace or reject, with feedback on  their selection (for example – motivating and unmotivating sentences, balanced and unbalanced thoughts); and mirror card game, in which the user either selects a topic or has one selected automatically ("Choose for me") and then receives a set of cards, each containing two questions for personal reflection.
Figure X.   Example Mindset Activity: Breathing Exercise
Figure X.   Example Mindset Activity: Reflection Activation Game
Figure X.   Example Mindset Activity: Inner Voice
Figure X.   Example Mindset Activity: Mirror Card Game
Activities are initially delivered in a predetermined sequence. As the user progresses and is introduced to the available tools and activations, the program transitions to a choice-based model in which the user selects from thematic categories based on personal relevance. These categories include topics such as ‘Take a breather’, ‘Relaxation’, ‘Mindfulness’, ‘Self-Care’, ‘Flexible Thinking’, ‘Attention & Emotional Balance’, ‘Cultivating calm’, ‘Meaningful action’, and ‘In the moment’. Each category presents a curated grouping of activities, tailored to the theme of that category. This progressive structure is designed to first familiarize the user with the full range of available techniques and then empower them to direct their own practice based on individual needs and preferences.
Before each activity, the user sees an introductory page that introduces the activity and provides any guidance needed ahead of performing the activity (e.g. find a comfortable spot, consider using headphones). 
Additional App Features
Personalized Messages & Reminders
To promote engagement with the PD-002 treatment protocol, the PD-002 app includes a multimodal messaging system that delivers personalized messages to the user in-app as well as reminders via phone notifications and text messages, and a weekly email. 
In-app messages, phone notifications, text messages, and email are all generated using generative intelligence (GenAI) systems that utilize a fixed prompt and versioned LLM to personalize
